Full `bun run check` GREEN (tsc + lint + vitest). **Self-reviewed, no independent reviewer** — one Explore sub-agent mapped the trigger/attack.ts seams and confirmed the template, and the new trigger rides the just-touched attack.ts spot. `/code-review` still NOT run (user-triggered; D96 + D97 + D98 + this slice all await it). *Why: D98 split the `onDamagedByAttack` label into "passive-shaped" (counters) and "genuinely trigger-shaped" (status/parking-discard); this closes the FIRST trigger-shaped card by building exactly the framework D98 named as the follow-up — reusing D98's scan spot means the Burn variant is a small honest addition (a timing, a helper, a card, a fixture), and the parking Klawf ex stays deferred as the one card that needs more.* (2026-07-27) |
| D100 | `disableAbilities` — the continuous Ability-lock AURA, the first passive that reaches OTHER Pokémon, gating all four Ability read sites (P3-M5, engine 0.51.0) | The resume point's recommended "widest coverage" row, and the backlog's biggest blast radius. **Verbatim re-confirmed against the live D1 before authoring** (the D95→D99 lesson): one query (`abilities_json LIKE '%have no Abilities%'`) returned EXACTLY the six ids the registry now carries and nothing else — **Klefki sv01-096 "Mischievous Lock"** ("As long as this Pokémon is in the Active Spot, Basic Pokémon in play (both yours and your opponent's) have no Abilities, except for Mischievous Lock."), **Spiritomb sv02-089 "Fettered in Misfortune"** ("Basic Pokémon V in play (both yours and your opponent's) have no Abilities." — no Active-Spot clause, so it locks from the BENCH), **Ting-Lu ex sv02-127/-243/-263/-275 "Cursed Land"** ("As long as this Pokémon is in the Active Spot, your opponent's Pokémon in play that have any damage counters on them have no Abilities, except for Pokémon ex."). A second query confirmed no other phrasing of the lock exists in the pool, and that sv01-129 — the OTHER Spiritomb — has no Ability at all (a pinned negative test). **Modelled as ONE new `PassiveEffects` field `disableAbilities?: {stage?, suffix?, side, requiresDamage?, requiresActive?, exemptSuffix?, exemptAbilityNamed?}`** — seven independent narrowing predicates that between them express all three printed sentences, no new op / timing / action / phase. **But it is the FIRST passive field that does not modify its HOLDER** — it reaches other Pokémon — so continuous.ts reads it through a dedicated both-boards pass, `disabledAbilityUids(state)`, returning the set of top uids whose Abilities are off; only a TOP CARD grants an aura (it is a printed Pokémon Ability, never a Tool). **Four read sites consult that Set by uid:** activated (`cardplay.ts useAbility` → the new `ABILITY_DISABLED` error, checked BEFORE the activeOnly/oncePerTurn/cost gates so a locked Pokémon reports the LOCK rather than an incidental refusal), passive (`continuous.ts passivesOf` — drops the top card's printed passive only; the holder's attached **Tools keep working**, they are §7.4 card effects and not Abilities), triggered (`triggers.ts triggersOf` — the single choke covering onPlayToBench / onEvolve / betweenTurns / onDamagedByAttack; **onKnockOut is deliberately NOT gated**, it fires as the Pokémon leaves play) and the HUD (`redact.ts redactedAbilitiesOf` — the row greys with `reason: null`, self-evident like the Active-only greying, so the client never offers a button the engine will refuse). **Auras are collected UNGATED — a lock never turns itself, or another lock, off.** Self-exemption is what the printed text asks for (Klefki's `exemptAbilityNamed`, matched on the TARGET card's printed Ability name, so a mirror match leaves both locks on); lock-vs-lock is the **KNOWN LIMITATION**: an Active Ting-Lu ex opposite a damaged Klefki should by the rules switch Mischievous Lock off, and does not — that needs a fixpoint pass rather than one read, and is a documented follow-up **pinned by a tripwire test** that asserts the current behaviour and says to flip when the fixpoint lands. The three cards in scope never mute a NON-lock ability of another lock's source, so the limitation only bites lock-vs-lock. **Tests:** `packages/engine/src/abilityLock.test.ts` (19) — the registry row (all six ids + the sv01-129 negative); the aura scan as a set-membership matrix (empty with no lock in play — the no-op guarantee; Klefki locking every Basic on BOTH boards while skipping a Stage 1 and itself; Klefki dark from the Bench; the mirror match; Spiritomb locking Basic V on both boards FROM THE BENCH and MISSING a VMAX — a suffix match, not a prefix one; Ting-Lu reaching only the opponent's damaged non-ex, with its own damaged bench, an undamaged opponent and a damaged opposing **ex** all clear; Ting-Lu dark from the Bench; the lock-vs-lock tripwire); then a **lock-ON / lock-OFF pair per read site** — `ABILITY_DISABLED` vs the `ABILITY_ACTIVE_ONLY` the same call falls back to (the check-ORDER proof), Cursed Land flipping a Stage 2's activated Ability the instant it takes one counter (Tinkaton is out of both Basic-only locks' reach, so that pair is Cursed Land's alone), Bouffalant's Bouffer suppressed (the same printed 30 lands as 30 vs 10), a locked attacker's Vitality Band still adding its 10 (the Tool exemption), Armarouge's `onDamagedByAttack` Burn suppressed vs firing, and the HUD row greyed vs enabled. **The implementation needed NO behavioural fix** — 18 of 19 passed on the first run and the 19th was a seed whose deck had drawn its Klefki. Fixture work this session: HP/retreat/stage corrected against the live prints (Spiritomb 60, Ting-Lu ex 240/4), and `ABILITY_LOCK_DECK` rebuilt to carry one target per read site AND per predicate field — its `board()` helper **asserts both seats open on the neutral fix-bigbody**, because this deck holds three aura sources and two Pokémon V and any other opening Active would smuggle a live aura onto the board and silently poison every set assertion. Klefki's fixture carries fix-attacker's plain Bite ({C}, 30) instead of its printed "Joust" ({C}, 10 + an unsimulated Tool discard) — a DELIBERATE, commented deviation: Klefki must be the Active to emit its aura, so it must be the attacker, and the lock-ON/lock-OFF arms have to compare the same printed 30. No web/API/DB/schema change. engineVersion 0.50.0 → **0.51.0**; 142 → **143** files, 1997 → **2016** tests. Full `bun run check` GREEN (tsc + lint + vitest). **Self-reviewed, no independent reviewer**; `/code-review` still NOT run (user-triggered; D96 + D97 + D98 + D99 + this slice all await it). *Why: the widest row was worth taking before the narrow leftovers because the cost is in the READ SITES, not the cards — once every ability read consults one Set, later locks are registry rows. Landing it as a predicate on the existing passive field (rather than new machinery) kept the diff to one scan function plus four one-line gates, and the honest cost is named rather than hidden: the aura-vs-aura fixpoint is deferred WITH a failing-when-fixed tripwire instead of being quietly wrong.* (2026-07-28) |

## Locked assumptions (override explicitly if they change)
- Bun-workspace monorepo; API + Lobby DO on Cloudflare **Workers** via `wrangler`.
- **Hono** + **Zod**; **Drizzle** over D1. Ingest validates every payload with
  **our own Zod schemas** and defaults to **plain REST fetch** — the
  2026-07-09 finding that the official `@tcgdex/sdk` is *unnecessary for
  validation* still stands, and is why its types are never the boundary.
  **Amended 2026-08-04 (D188):** the SDK is now an installed, opt-in
  **transport** (`--transport=sdk`), pinned `2.9.0` in `apps/api` only; the
  fetch+Zod posture is unchanged and remains the default.
- Server **sessions** (http-only cookie), not stateless JWT.
- Ingest filters to SV-era but writes the full-history schema.
- attacks/weaknesses/resistances stored as JSON columns for now (promote to
  child tables only if we need to query inside them).
- English (`en`) first; schema leaves room for i18n later.
- The **match engine (P3)** is the actual gameplay; approximate at first,
  improved iteratively.

## These are defaults, not law
Every decision and assumption here is a **default with a rationale**, chosen with
the context available at the time — revisit any of them when the code or new
context reveals a better path. The point of writing them down is to preserve the
*why*, so a later session can judge whether it still holds.

## Adding / changing a decision
Append a row (or a dated subsection for bigger ones) with the choice **and the
one-line why**. When you revise an existing decision, update its row and note
what changed and why. The one hard rule: **don't reverse a decision silently** —
leave a trail so the reasoning is never lost.
| D101 | `onDamagedByAttack` PARKING — Klawf ex "Counterattacking Pincer", the reactive trigger that PARKS an opponent-side discard during the attacker's turn, closing the row 4/4 (P3-M5, engine 0.52.0) | The last card on the `onDamagedByAttack` row, and the one D98/D99 deferred as "needs the parking path, not more timing". **Verbatim re-confirmed against the live D1** (the D95→D100 lesson; a query on `abilities_json LIKE '%damaged by an attack%'` re-fixed the family boundary — Cacnea/Cacturne/Stunfisk done by D98, Armarouge by D99, Fezandipiti sv06.5-073 out of scope): Klawf ex **sv03-120** "Counterattacking Pincer" — "If this Pokémon is in the Active Spot and is damaged by an attack from your opponent's Pokémon (even if this Pokémon is Knocked Out), discard an Energy from the Attacking Pokémon." (Basic Fighting, 220 HP, retreat 3.) **Its reaction is `discardEnergy from:"opponentActive"` (Mawile's op, reused verbatim, `filter: anyEnergy`) run under the DAMAGED seat** — so `discardVictimSeat(damagedSeat)=otherSeat` reaches the ATTACKER's Active, and the DEFENDER chooses which Energy. That choice must PARK during the OPPONENT's turn, which D99's inline non-parking `runDamagedByAttackTriggers` (`.state`-only) could not carry. **Two code-map sub-agents surfaced the clean fit: the `koTrigger` stage, not the `answerer` mechanism.** The whole reactive program belongs to the non-turn player, so — exactly like `runKoTrigger` (which runs on-KO programs during the opponent's turn with `controller = koedSeat`) — the program is folded through settleProgram **under the DAMAGED seat** (`controller = damagedSeat`), making it the answerer by default (`phase.seat = damagedSeat`, NO `decider`/`answerer` needed); the projection reads the real turn owner off the attackEpilogue in `pending` (`koParkActiveSeat`, which already recognises that stage). **Modelled as a new `damagedTrigger` PendingStage** `{seat, uid}` (the twin of `koTrigger`): attack.ts records it at damage time — only when the damaged Active carries such an Ability (via the new `damagedByAttackAbility` gated lookup, which applies the §9 ability-lock through `triggersOf` and the "in the Active Spot" clause), so every other damaging attack keeps its exact pre-slice queue — and seeds it AFTER the attack's own effect program but BEFORE the attackEpilogue: `[damagedTrigger, attackEpilogue]`. flow.ts `runDamagedTrigger` (mirrors `runKoTrigger`) pops itself, runs the program, folds through settleProgram with `resumeTail`; a PARK leaves the attackEpilogue behind it, and resolveEffect (DEFENDER-only, via the existing seat gate) resumes it → finishAttack's §8.1 sweep + turn end. **"Even if Knocked Out" stays free** (the stage precedes the sweep, so the lookup finds Klawf still Active), and Klawf ex being a rule-box ex prizes 2 (D93). **D99's `runDamagedByAttackTriggers` was replaced by `damagedByAttackAbility`; Armarouge's non-parking Burn now rides the SAME staged path — verified byte-identical (scorchingArmor.test.ts 4/4 green unchanged).** Reordering the trigger from "before the effect program" (D99's inline spot) to "after it, as a stage" is also more rules-correct (an attack fully resolves before its damage's reactive triggers). **No web/API/DB/schema/redaction change** — the discard candidates are the attacker's face-up Energy (public-ref family), the park's answerer defaults to `phase.seat = damagedSeat`, and `phaseView`/`redact` already handle the on-KO shape. **Tests:** `packages/engine/src/counterattackingPincer.test.ts` (8) — the registry authoring; the park (phase.seat=p2, `answerer` absent, `resumeTail` true, discardable = the attacker's Active Energy); the projection (activeSeat=attacker, waitingSeat=defender); the attacker CANNOT answer (WRONG_SEAT — the routing proof); the defender's pick discarding from the attacker + turn end; "even if KO'd" (park before the sweep, discard before KNOCKED_OUT, ko:takePrizes p1 count 2); the `dealt>0` gate (Yawn → no reaction, attacker keeps both Energy); (`SetModel` additionally rebuilds `set.cards` as class instances each carrying an `sdk` back-reference, making the model **non-JSON-serialisable**; the raw payload is.) **DISCREPANCIES BETWEEN THE SDK's TYPES AND OUR SCHEMAS — the most valuable output of the slice.** The SDK's `Card` type declares **NO `pricing`, NO `updated`, NO `variants_detailed`** — all three are present on **every** committed card fixture, and **`updated` is written to D1 by `mapCard`**, so adopting the SDK type as the mapper's input would have dropped a column. `Set` declares no `abbreviation` (live sv01: `{"official":"SVI"}`); `Serie` declares only `{id,name,logo?,sets}` (live `sv` also has `releaseDate`/`firstSet`/`lastSet`); `variants` omits `wPromo`; `VariantsDetailed` omits `pricing` and makes `variantId` required. In the other direction the SDK is **wrong-strict**: `Card.item` is typed `{name: string; effect: string}` (both required) while live **dp5-4 serves `item: {}`**; `abilities[].type`/`.effect` are required but our schema has seen them absent. And `Card.category` is plain `string`, not the three-way literal our discriminated union needs — LOOSER, which is the safe direction, as are the SDK's required `rarity`/`legal` against our optional ones (our schema is the more liberal, so nothing the SDK can serve is rejected). **THE CONVENIENCE CLAIM IS SMALLER THAN IT LOOKS, AND SAYING SO IS THE POINT.** The SDK offers **no whole-set fetching**: `fetchCards(setId)` merely returns `set.cards`, the same card *resumes* the full `/sets/{id}` payload already contains — **not** full card detail — so the N sequential per-card detail requests remain necessary and the run's request count is unchanged. It also adds **no pacing and no backoff**, only a per-URL in-process cache, so **the seam owns the 50 ms spacing for BOTH transports** and the politeness posture is identical either way. What the SDK genuinely buys: URL/language construction, a versioned user-agent, endpoint validation, and an upstream that tracks API changes. ⚠️ **WHAT IS PROVEN AND WHAT IS NOT.** Proven here: the package installs and typechecks; `new TCGdex("en")` is inert; the SDK's HTTP layer really executes under bun (it issued a real request and received a real 403); both transports issue the right requests, hand payloads on **by identity** (asserted with `toBe`, so nothing is cloned or reshaped), fail loudly, and pace identically; the CLI's flag parsing rejects `--transport=bogus` instead of falling back. **NOT proven: a single successful call to `api.tcgdex.net` — no live request was possible in this session, so `--transport=sdk` has never returned a real payload.** The untestable part is isolated to one named function, `createDefaultSdkClient`. The command that discharges this on a networked machine is **`cd apps/api && bun scripts/ingest.ts --sets sve --dry-run --transport=sdk`** (24 cards, writes SQL, applies nothing), then the same without `--dry-run`. **DRIFT DETECTORS, NOT PROSE:** `sdkContract.test.ts` pins each omission with **`@ts-expect-error`**, which TypeScript errors on when *unused* — so the day the SDK starts declaring `Card.updated` (or any of the others), `bun run check` FAILS and someone re-reads the findings. Verified by deliberately pointing one at a field that *does* exist and confirming `error TS2578: Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive`. `source.ts` lives under `src/` (so it typechecks and is unit-tested with stubs) but is **deliberately NOT re-exported from the `src/ingest/` barrel**, and the CLI imports it by path, so the SDK cannot reach the Worker bundle through the barrel; the CLI itself stays outside tsconfig's `include`, as before. **215 → 217 test files, 3948 → 3976 tests, `bun run check` GREEN.** *Why: the user wanted the official SDK, and the honest way to give it to them was to put it exactly where it helps — the wire — and nowhere near the one property that keeps bad data out of D1. The slice's real product is the list of six places where the SDK's types and the live payloads disagree, which is only visible because we kept parsing.* |

This attack's damage isn't affected by Weakness."*) moved `OPAQUE` → `COMPOUND-head`, because its HEAD now builds — the instrument reporting the remaining blockers (a Weakness-ONLY `DAMAGE_SUPPRESSION` arm that does not exist, and a splitter that requires an EFFECT tail) instead of shrugging. Both are true statements about one guard, and they disagree only because of ORDER: the narrowing arm ships FIRST, so the guard is the only thing standing between it and a string the older arm owns, and removing it changes an answer. Move the arm behind the pattern it narrows and the guard stops doing work — the swap is equivalent precisely because in THAT order the lookahead is unobservable, which is also the order in which the deletion row would have survived vacuously and been mistaken for a declared equivalence. **So a guard's killability is a property of the dispatch order, not of the guard.** The corpus can only see a narrowing predicate when the narrow pattern runs first; ship it second and the same three lines are untestable by construction while looking identical in review.
